title: betaLB
text: Generated files may stay Overleaf regular files, never links; template change reaches Overleaf project’s next upload (Verify() skips ). Keep Makefile, project.Rproj, .gitignore files, scripts project’s build uses. Remove .setup/scripts/* except project.R. copy without Makefile: Rscript -e 'rProject::Template(getwd())' , make.

title: betaLB
text: Files .setup/r-dependencies/ Overleaf links private functions repository (<lib>/<file> ), shared projects. Never edit project put upload folder. change one, edit local functions clone (next projects; agents never push) write upload folder functions; test, copy files scratch build project, project. Order: functions first; refresh links project push. reply log name links refresh. make linked compares files functions clone (FUNCTIONS=<path>).

title: betaLB
text: Overleaf’s GitHub sync stops 7 MB editable text caps text files 2 MB. Keep large data compressed (binary, e.g. .Rds .xz) never store file twice. make sizecheck reports problems.

title: betaLB
text: Every exported function roxygen documentation tests. make runs checks; fix every error, warning, note. Keep R style rules global instructions (BigCamelCase, one function per file, internal .Foo functions R/<pkg>-<name>-dot.R).

title: betaLB
text: package CRAN headed . R CMD check ---cran must pass errors, warnings, notes, R release R devel. Every user-visible change: version bump NEWS.md entry. Examples, tests, vignettes write tempdir(), use two cores, need internet unless skipped (skip_on_cran(), skip_if_offline()). Long examples go \donttest{}. submission: cran-comments.md (test environments, check results, reverse dependencies) reverse-dependency checks package . user submits CRAN. Agents prepare submission; never submit.

title: Likelihood-Based Confidence Intervals for Regression Effect Sizes
text: Generates profile likelihood confidence intervals standardized regression coefficients (beta) effect sizes, including multiple correlation, semipartial correlations, improvement R-squared, squared partial correlations, differences standardized regression coefficients, Cohen’s f-squared, models fitted lm().

title: Likelihood-Based Confidence Intervals for Regression Effect Sizes
text: can install development version betaLB GitHub :
code: if (!requireNamespace(package = "pak", quietly = TRUE)) {   utils::install.packages(pkgs = "pak") } pak::pkg_install(pkg = "jeksterslab/betaLB")

title: Likelihood-Based Confidence Intervals for Regression Effect Sizes
text: Fit effect families, calibration types confidence levels needed. Extractors select stored results without refitting. Scalar targets use profile-likelihood regions. Multi-coefficient R-squared block effects use conservative vector projection; output identifies calibration dimension. Robust calibration assumes independently sampled random regressors finite fourth moments. supply fixed-regressor clustered-data inference. $intervals contains every computed band endpoint statuses. $diagnostics retains numerical verification details. unverified endpoint NA; Wald endpoint substituted. Adjusted R-squared explicitly sample-size-dependent transformation, interval can negative lower bound.
code: fit <- stats::lm(formula = mpg ~ wt + hp, data = mtcars) out <- betaLB::LB(   object = fit,   effects = c("beta", "rsq"),   type = c("mvn", "robust"),   alpha = c(0.05, 0.10) ) betaLB::BetaLB(object = out) #> Call: #> betaLB::LB(object = fit, type = c("mvn", "robust"), alpha = c(0.05,  #>     0.1), effects = c("beta", "rsq")) #>  #> Likelihood intervals (vector projections are conservative) #> type = "mvn, robust" #>   effect   type alpha estimate   lower   upper lower_status upper_status #> 1     wt    mvn  0.05  -0.6296 -0.7934 -0.4347           ok           ok #> 2     wt    mvn  0.10  -0.6296 -0.7691 -0.4683           ok           ok #> 3     wt robust  0.05  -0.6296 -0.7579 -0.4831           ok           ok #> 4     wt robust  0.10  -0.6296 -0.7385 -0.5079           ok           ok #> 5     hp    mvn  0.05  -0.3615 -0.5538 -0.1628           ok           ok #> 6     hp    mvn  0.10  -0.3615 -0.5231 -0.1959           ok           ok #> 7     hp robust  0.05  -0.3615 -0.4911 -0.2297           ok           ok #> 8     hp robust  0.10  -0.3615 -0.4703 -0.2512           ok           ok #>      calibration dimension #> 1 scalar_profile         1 #> 2 scalar_profile         1 #> 3 scalar_profile         1 #> 4 scalar_profile         1 #> 5 scalar_profile         1 #> 6 scalar_profile         1 #> 7 scalar_profile         1 #> 8 scalar_profile         1 stats::confint(object = betaLB::RSqLB(object = out), type = "robust") #>         lower     upper #> rsq 0.6661115 0.9146316 #> adj 0.6430847 0.9087442

title: Likelihood Intervals for Regression Effect Sizes — LB
text: object Unweighted, full-rank scalar-response lm fit intercept, stored model frame, offsets positive residual variance. type Character vector containing mvn, robust, . alpha Distinct significance levels (0, 1). effects Requested families: beta, rsq, scor, pcor, deltarsq, diffbeta, fsq. std_y Whether standardize response slope targets. std_x Logical flags names model-matrix predictors standardize slope targets. effects keep definitions. blocks Named list additional predictor blocks, identified model-matrix column names indices, increments local f-squared. control Named list: maxeval native evaluation budget per endpoint; tolerance normalized verification tolerance.

title: Likelihood Intervals for Regression Effect Sizes — LB
text: Context class lb, containing named point estimates, long intervals table per-row endpoint diagnostics. Failed endpoints NA specific status. Extractors return betalb objects. Slope/contrast target IDs retain standardization flags.

title: Likelihood Intervals for Regression Effect Sizes — LB
text: Normal theory uses divisor-n Gaussian covariance likelihood. Robust calibration uses empirical fourth moments. Signed scalar targets use target-specific variance ratio; multi-coefficient nonnegative effects use conservative vector projection largest-eigenvalue robust cutoff. asymptotic procedures, without finite-sample coverage guarantee.
